title: Sigismund August, Frater Georg and Queen Isabella to Ibrahim Pasha, 1548 (HHStA Wien StAbt Türkei I 7-4-4, 7-4-5, 7-4-9; catalogue 885)

plaintext.source: The Latin exemplar on f. 30 (image 4) filed with the two cipher copies (f. 28, f. 29).

transcription.notes: f. 29 (copy A) transcribed sign by sign, 13 lines, 572 signs including 21 null words, by two image agents on 30 Oct 2026 (transcription/f29_lines_01-07.txt, f29_lines_08-13.txt). The agents had the Latin exemplar open, so values marked * come from it and unmarked values may be biased toward it; a blind re-transcription has not been made. f. 28 and the 7-4-5 copies not transcribed. Blind check of lines 8-10: 61.4% match against the exemplar vs 99.2% crib-assisted (transcription/blind/RESULT.md); use 61% as the independent fit. 31 Oct 2026 (PR #196): f. 28 transcribed sign by sign from a 932 px viewer screenshot (transcription/r367/f28_signs.txt) and f. 29 re-checked (f29_signs_recheck.txt); both copies deciphered with R367, plaintext in reading_full.txt (744A, 744D).

documents.shelfmark: Wien, Haus-, Hof- und Staatsarchiv, StAbt Türkei I 7-4-9 (AIS 7040845), f. 51-59
documents.route: Giovanni Maria Malvezzi (Constantinople) -> Ferdinand I; enclosed copies of two Frater Georg letters to Ibrahim Pasha (Corde, 28 July; Monostor, 22 July 1548)

plaintext.source: A contemporary interlinear Italian decipherment over every cipher line of the original letter (texts/gloss_7-4-9_letter.txt). The replica and the two enclosures have none.

transcription.source: AIS bildansicht viewer, screenshots from a cloud browser (about 930-1565 px)
transcription.notes: Letter units L1-L6 and enclosures B and C transcribed sign by sign, 30-31 Oct 2026 (transcription/r367/7-4-9_*_signs.txt); the gloss transcribed separately and compared after each unit was read from the signs. The replica (f. 53-54) not transcribed. Sign counts not measured: the sign files mix formats.

system.summary: Graphic-sign homophonic cipher with nulls and a code list: the Ferdinand-Malvezzi key of 1548 (DECODE R367), which reads every copy.
system.notes: R367 confirmed on all 14 cipher units (31 Oct 2026). This hand: crossed-tail 9 = r, smooth-tail 9 = x (KEY_BRIEF has them reversed); h-hook = n; lambda = h; plain Pi and Sha = g; footed circle = q; loose nulls also written inside words. Code groups not in R367: Mos, Mes, Mus, Ris, za, Ses, yu, 59, 68, Ko (meanings from the 7-4-9 gloss or context). See NOTES.md.

prior_solution.where: The Latin exemplars of 7-4-4 and 7-4-5 are filed with the cipher copies (f. 30, f. 34), and the 7-4-9 letter carries a contemporary interlinear decipherment. The 7-4-9 enclosures B and C have no plaintext here. No modern decipherment found (repository, DECODE, AIS, web, 29 Oct 2026); Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 not seen.

conditions.human_role: Harrison Bornstein reported the target and the candidate key (PR #196); Daniel Bourdeau reviewed it, pointed out that the scans are public, and asked for the sign test and R367 against the exemplars; Harry asked for the pass to be finished. No target-specific intervention in the reading.

solution.what: Contributor report (PR #196, Harrison Bornstein): AIS records are Reservatbestand, no images reachable; candidate key = malvezzi1548 R367. No decipherment found in the repository, the DECODE list, AIS or on the web.
Re-tested image access: the detail.aspx session cookie plus getimage.aspx returns the full scans despite 'Reservatbestand'. Fetched all 22 images of the three records.
Transcribed the Latin exemplars of 7-4-4 (f. 30) and 7-4-5 (exemplar C, f. 34) from the images.

Compared the first line of 7-4-4 f. 29 with the R367 key brief: Idcirco, b, d are listed nulls and the graphic signs match; the exemplar (about 560 letters) is the same order of length as the 13 cipher lines.
Cut 13 lines of f. 29 into 26 half-line crops (2x) and had two image agents transcribe them sign by sign, with the R367 key brief and the exemplar as crib; 572 signs, 80 sign labels, 6 left unknown.

Decoded f. 29 with the R367 values and aligned the result on the Latin exemplar (global alignment, align_f29.py). The cipher is the exemplar's text from 'Sigismundus Augustus' on, preceded by a short extra passage: 462 of 473 key-derived tokens (97.7%) match; 56 tokens depend on the exemplar and are not counted. The exemplar's heading is not enciphered.

Tabulated sign label against value: 80 labels, 15 with more than one value, the rest consistent. Two values differ from KEY_BRIEF.md (r and x look reversed; some pi and cup forms). No independent (blind) transcription has been made, so the match rate is an upper bound.

Blind check: one image agent transcribed f. 29 lines 8-10 from the crops and the R367 key files only (no exemplar, no crib). Against the exemplar segment its values match 70 of 114 scored tokens (61.4%), against 99.2% for the crib-assisted values of the same lines; the two transcriptions agree on 61 of 142 values. The key family is confirmed without the crib, but the earlier 97.7% overstated the independent fit.

The container proxy refused archivinformationssystem.at; opened the AIS viewer anonymously in a cloud browser and took screenshots of all 22 images of 7-4-4, 7-4-5 and 7-4-9, one page at a time (about 930-1565 px, below the 2400 px scans).
Compared sign shapes on f. 28, the 7-4-5 copies and 7-4-9 with k367.txt and KEY_BRIEF.md: the same repertoire and nulls throughout; the crossed-tail 9 is r and the smooth-tail 9 is x, as on f. 29.
f. 28 transcribed sign by sign (16 lines plus an interlinear header) and f. 29 re-checked at L01 and L11-L13.

Deciphered both 7-4-4 copies with R367: f. 28 enciphers the exemplar with its heading (not a longer text); f. 29 opens with 'replica'; the date clause reads 'Regni vero nostri ... ex commissione sacrae regiae Maiestatis propria'. 744A 84/94 read, 744D 82/92.
Transcribed exemplar B (f. 34r foot, f. 34v) and the four 7-4-5 cipher copies; they are two letters (B 6 June, C 2 July) in two copies each, the 'Dupl.' dockets on images 3 and 4 swapped.

Deciphered the four 7-4-5 copies with R367: 745B 115/130, 745X4 111/132, 745C 104/121, 745X3 102/118 read; the copies fill exemplar B's torn edge. Two signs not in the key (z of Chazum, a triple-barred x).

7-4-9: identified the original letter (Italian, cipher paragraphs L1-L6 with a contemporary interlinear decipherment), the replica, and enclosed copies B and C; transcribed the gloss and L1-L6 sign by sign.

Read L1-L6 from the signs before comparing the gloss: 424 words, 8 unread (7 small groups in L1, one blotted group in L2); new code groups Mos, Mes, Mus, Ris, za, Ses, yu, 59, 68 named from the gloss.
Enclosed copy B: a third Frater Georg letter (Corde, 28 July 1548), not either exemplar; 106 tokens, 65 read, 41 unread (tear, small signs, N. and F.).

Enclosed copy C, two passes: a fourth Frater Georg letter (Monostor, 22 July 1548) on the Sultan's tribute and the war near Eger; 214 tokens, 184 read, 30 unread (tear, ll. 16-23 at screenshot resolution, code Ko.).

Tried the README n-gram measure: gutenberg.org refused, so a stand-in 'la' corpus was built from Latin Library texts on GitHub. Calibration failed: malvezzi1548 scores 0.772 on it against 0.990 on the official corpus, so the n-gram figures here are low by about 20 points.

measure_sense.py: agreement with the external plaintext. 744/745, 687 words: 0.897 agree with the exemplar (0.940 with exemplar or n-gram); 749 letter, 395 plaintext words: 0.886 agree with the gloss (code words left out). Controls with letters shuffled within words: 0.108 and 0.034. Upper bounds: the exemplar and gloss were open to the reader.
